text: Healthy pigs normally stand up out of curiosity when someone approaches the pen; a group that stays asleep and gathered in a corner is a disease sign. Homogeneous body condition across a pen signals good management and health, while under-developed pigs mixed among a pen signal chronic disease or insufficient feed. All pigs should be made to stand to check for reluctance to rise or painful legs. Feeder observation shows whether animals are eating normally — seriously sick pigs stop eating. Coughing is easiest to detect as pigs stand and move when approached (especially in the morning); it cannot be assessed if pigs stay asleep. Check the floor (including under slatted floors) for diarrhea, and note constipation in pregnant sows as a sign worth investigating.
